backward_compat_traps.rule: MSB transmitted ONE SCK period AFTER WS changes.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Some 'I2S-like' variants (Left-Justified, Right-Justified, DSP mode) place the MSB ON the same edge as WS, not one cycle later. Mixing those variants with strict I2S receivers will appear as a 1-bit shift.

backward_compat_traps.rule: Target receiver latches WS + SD on the leading (LOW-to-HIGH) edge of SCK.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Some implementations latch on the trailing edge — incompatible with standard I2S receivers.

backward_compat_traps.rule: Transmitter and receiver may have different word lengths; mismatches are silently truncated or zero-padded — no error signal.
backward_compat_traps.trap: System integrators forget to configure receiver word length; resulting audio is silently wrong (gain change due to LSB truncation or padding).
Some 'TDM mode' and 'Left-Justified' variants use the OPPOSITE convention. Plugging an I2S codec into a Left-Justified transmitter swaps left and right channels silently.

previous_versions: v.1 (1 February 1986) — Initial Philips Semiconductors release.
v.2 (5 June 1996) — Second Philips Semiconductors release.
v.3 (17 February 2022) — Reconstructed from the original 1986/1996 spec by NXP Semiconductors; format updated; Master/Slave terminology updated to Controller/Target.

key_changes.summary: Editorial revisions to the original 1986 spec; same protocol behavior.
Reconstructed by NXP under the UM11732 document number with new identity guidelines; 'Master' → 'Controller' and 'Slave' → 'Target' for inclusive language; protocol behavior unchanged.

fields.version_naming_history_note: Originally Philips Semiconductors I2S Bus Specification (1986, revised 1996); NXP Semiconductors took over Philips Semiconductors in 2006; UM11732 (2022) is NXP's reconstruction of the original spec with updated language and identity. Industry-wide, 'I2S' has many sibling formats (Left-Justified, Right-Justified, TDM, DSP mode) that are often confused with strict I2S — only strict I2S follows UM11732's MSB-one-clock-after-WS rule.
